- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter part of the forecast, particularly when true values show a sharp decline or mean reversion.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward moves in history; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the final 5–10 days; true values often drop below forecasted mean.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the first 10 days; model tends to be 5–10% above true values.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; true values often dip before model adjusts.
- When history shows strong mean reversion, model holds onto overestimated values longer than warranted.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts become erratic after spikes, then drift downward too slowly.
- In cases of sustained upward trend, model tends to overfit the recent peak and fails to anticipate eventual correction.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes, especially in the final 5–7 days.
